_comment: The DISCRIMINATION pilot declaration for skillc#287 (orchestrator review, comment 6025311708, decisions P1-P6). Exploratory only: estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n() - draws NO verdict (operator ruling, comment 6021089903). Uses the 'discrimination-declaration' kind added to skillc.calibration by the separate calibration.py PR (branch feat-skillc-287-discrimination-declaration, Refs #287) - see that PR for why skillc.calibration.parse_declaration structurally cannot express this contrast, and _resolution_note below for what changed here as a result.
_resolution_note: This file previously carried kind 'discrimination-pilot-declaration' (not validated by skillc.calibration) with a _schema_note flagging the gap to the orchestrator. Ruling received (mailbox 5614/5626, 2026-10-06): add a real 'discrimination-declaration' kind to skillc.calibration instead of accounting this test purely through skillc#273's case-pairing records. This file now uses that kind: arms.degraded.subject.revision is the DERIVED label skillc.calibration._expected_degraded_revision computes (never typed), and arms.degraded.mutation carries the structured mutation (skill/path/removed_text/diagnose_evidence/mutated_digest) the schema requires. case-pairing (skillc#273) still produces the per-attempt record this study's counts read; the declaration-level identity/approval binding is now calibration.py's job, not case-pairing's.

pilot.purpose: exploratory - estimates p_hat_intact and p_hat_degraded for evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's choose_n(); draws no verdict
pilot.no_verdict_statement: This pilot draws no DISCRIMINATING / NOT_SHOWN / UNKNOWN verdict. Its 10 attempts per arm are too few to be the predeclared discrimination test itself (that test is the MAIN study's schedule, sized by this pilot's results) and are never pooled into the main study's counts (P1).
rule_citations: P1 (comment 6025311708): pilot attempts never count toward the main study.

P2 (comment 6025311708): the pilot uses the same two-declaration shape, one pilot declaration per test, each 2-arm at n=10, each separately approved at 10. The intact arm therefore runs in both pilot declarations (see pilot-improvement-declaration.json's 'intact' arm, same subject).

P3 (comment 6025311708): this pilot's own raw proportions (passes/evaluable) must never be plugged into the sizing simulation directly - convert with evals/calibration-287/power_simulation.py's jeffreys_estimate() first.
P5 (comment 6025311708): tolerance is max(1, ceil(0.05*n)) per arm, not a flat 1.

P6 (comment 6025311708): arm order is calibration's seed-derived interleaving, so the two arms run interleaved in time rather than as two blocks - skillc.calibration.derive_arm_order, called by skillc.calibration.parse_discrimination_declaration itself now, not merely reused as an external scheduling utility.
